title: Evidence-Based Treatment with Botulinum Toxin and Strengthening Interdisciplinary Cooperation in the Management of Patients with Post-Stroke Spasticity - moVe-it
summary:
Background: Up to 40% of people develop muscle stiffness (spasticity) after a stroke. This condition can cause pain, limit movement, reduce independence in everyday life, and increase the need for care. Although effective treatments such as botulinum toxin injections and physiotherapy are recommended in medical guidelines, they are often not used consistently in routine care. At the same time, the number of people affected by stroke is expected to rise due to an aging population. To improve care for these patients, a new digitally supported care program was developed as part of the moVe-it study.
Research Question: The moVe-it study aims to find out whether digital care management can help ensure that recommended treatments are used more often, improve coordination between healthcare providers, and enhance patients’ health and quality of life. The study also examines how well this new approach can be integrated into everyday healthcare practice and whether it influences the use of medical services.
Methods: A total of 520 patients with stroke-related spasticity will take part in the cluster-randomized controlled moVe-it study in Bavaria, Berlin, and Brandenburg. Patients can join either during a hospital stay or after discharge. Participants in the intervention group receive structured, digitally supported care. This includes regular case discussions between healthcare professionals, coordination of treatment by a medical manager, and support through the dedicated moVe-it app. The control group receives usual medical care and access to a simplified version of the app. To evaluate the program, patients will complete questionnaires and undergo physical examinations at several time points over eight months. These assessments will be conducted by staff members who are not aware of patients' treatment group.

interventions.name:
Intervention
Participants in the intervention group will receive access to a new model of care in the form of a digitally supported care management program. This program comprises interdisciplinary case conferences, care coordination provided by the moVe-it-medical-manager, and study-related suppor

Control group
Patients will receive therapeutic measures within the framework of standard care at the discretion of the treating physicians, as well as access to the moVe-it App in a simplified format (light version).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1- Relevant spasticity (G81.1, G82.1, G82.4, G81.9) following stroke (I60*, I61*, I63*, I64*, I69*); assessed by treating practitioner
2- The stroke must not have occurred more than twelve months prior to inclusion
3- Patients treated by participating healthcare providers
4- Availability of an email address and an internet-enabled smartphone. If technically feasible, support by relatives is permitted
5- Statutory health insurance coverage
6- Signed declaration of participation/informed consent form provided by the patient
Exclusion criteria:
1- Language or neurocognitive barriers that preclude study participation
2- Insufficient proficiency in the German language if valid participation in study-related questionnaires and informed consent discussions is not possible
3- Concurrent participation in another interventional study
4- Residence outside the study region
5- Private health insurance coverage (implementation of the new model of care is provided by statutory health insurance funds within the framework of a selective contract pursuant to Section 140a of the SGB V or a treatment contract pursuant to Sections 630a–c of the BGB)
6- Other medical or ethical reasons that, in the justified assessment of the treating physician, preclude participation; the decision must be documented
